reason: Conversation 1 correctly framed the symptom as a sump/pump issue, walked the homeowner through condenser removal and a more thorough sump flush, then devised a practical cup-of-water test when they said they couldn't recognise pump noise, while keeping the pump-vs-blockage question honestly open and pointing to an engineer if the test failed. Conversation 2 did say 'unplug first' but then wasted turns on an irrelevant drum-warmth check (the customer rightly pushed back since it already heats), suggested checking a drain hose at the rear the customer had already said was inaccessible, and ended by declaring the pump needs replacing with a parts panel despite no model number and the ground truth being genuinely uncertain. Conversation 1's only gaps were an early tilt suggestion before learning it was stacked and no explicit unplug reminder, neither of which outweighs Conversation 2's inefficiency and overconfident part call.
